segments.text: And we will begin. Good morning everyone. Thank you for being here at the Commission this morning.
This is the Tuesday, September the 1st, 2026 administrative session of the Georgia Public
Service Commission. Turning our attention first to the utility consent agenda. Would any
Commissioner like any item on the consent agenda held or moved to the regular agenda?
Hearing no request, all in favor of approving the items on the consent agenda say aye.
Aye. Aye. Any opposed? The consent agenda passes unanimously. Moving on to the regular agenda,
does any Commissioner wish for any item to be held? All right, we'll start and we'll take up R1 first.
Good morning Leon. Good morning sir. R1 is docket 5662A. Consideration of request filed by GMA to modify
the cost allocation filing deadline. Staff recommends it be extended from 90 to 180 days.
Staff recommends it be approved. Okay, thank you Leon. Commissioners, any questions on R1?
All right, you've heard staff's recommendation on R1. All in favor say aye. Aye. Any opposed?
R1 passes unanimously. R2. R2 is docket 36946. Consideration of request for universal service
certification by the following ETCs AAAA through UU. This is an annual certification that they will
use high-cost funding the way it's supposed to be used. Staff recommends approval. Okay,
any questions on R2? All right, you've heard staff's recommendation on R2. All in favor say aye.
Aye. Aye. Any opposed? R2 passes unanimously. Move on to R3. Morning Tony.
Item R3 is docket number 43510 and the Atlanta Gaslight Company's universal service fund
facilities expansion plan and docket number 41559 Econ 1 tariff projects.
Consideration of the Dawson-Lumpkin County project. Part A of the USF recovery presentation
is the USF recovery presentation. Part B is the Econ 1 recovery presentation
and that will be presented by Jamie Shavey and part C is staff's proposed order.
Regarding the USF recovery on July 27, 2026, AGL filed the project with an engineering estimate
of $64.6 million. The staff decided to split the engineering estimate recovery
with 50% from the USF and 50% from Econ 1 or $32.3 million each. The staff reviewed the seven USF
MFRs and found them to be whole and complete. With income taxes and finance costs, the total
USF recovery is $37.5 million. The staff recommends the following USF recovery. First, the staff
recommends approval of the Dawson-Lumpkin County project with a total engineering estimate of
$64.6 million and with a USF recovery amount of $37.5 million. That includes income taxes and
finance costs. Second, the staff recommends that the project be approved as a multi-year USF project
with the annual allotments found in table two of staff's backup. Third, the staff recommends
that the quarterly reporting be filed in both docket number 43510 and 4159.
Fourth, the staff recommends that through AGL's engineering review process if the project has a
10% change in the cost to serve engineering estimate found that MFR 6 or a change in the
project technical analysis found in MFR 7 or a change in the proposed route provided in MFR 1,
the written description, or MFR 4, the maps. AGL will file a report with the commission providing
details why the changes took place. Janie will provide the R1 Part B presentation.
Any questions for Mr. Wackerly? Okay. Thank you, Tony. Janie?
Good morning. Good morning, commissioners. For Part B, the Econ1 portion, on July 27,
2026, Atlanta Gaslight also filed for approval of these projects under the Econ1 tariff.
In Dawson County, the company is proposing to provide service to poultry farms under the AG1
rate class. The poultry farms are commercial operations, many of which will provide stock
to large poultry processors and will be liquid propane gas, LP gas, conversion projects.
The estimated customer capital investment is $100,000. Under the AG1 rate class,
the requirement of additional jobs to the local community and the anticipated tax base
are not applicable. The farms will add 100 decatherms per year of connected load.
In Lumpkin County, Atlanta Gaslight Company will serve Structure Outdoor LLC,
a customer in the Lumpkin Industrial Park under the G11 rate class.
Structure manufactures structures for use in the outdoor living industry.
Structure is also an LP gas conversion project. Natural gas will be used for space heating and
manufacturing processes. The estimated capital investment is $7 million. Structure will add
50 jobs and the anticipated tax base will be $160,000. Structure will add 7,800 decatherms
per year of connected load. And finally, Atlanta Gaslight will also serve Satellite Industries,
a manufacturer in Lumpkin County. Satellite Industries is a portable toilet manufacturer
that will use natural gas for space heating, water heating, and manufacturing processes.
Satellite is also an LP conversion process project. The customer capital investment is $25 million.
Satellite will add 80 jobs and the anticipated tax base will be $20,000. Satellite will add
5,000 decatherms per year of connected load. Staff reviewed the minimum filing requirements.
The information was found to be whole, complete, and in compliance.
The Econ1 tariff has an annual cap of $25 million. To accommodate the $32,333,837
and $57.50 requested costs, the cost must be allocated over two years, 2026 and 2027.
The balance of the 2026 Econ1 rider allocation is $18,591,760. The entirety
of which can be applied to the project. The remaining $13,742,077.50 will be applied toward
the 2027 Econ1 rider, leaving $11,257,922.50 available for future projects.
Staff recommends approval of the Dawson Lumpkin projects in the allocation amounts provided
for 2026 and 2027. Thank you, Janie. Commissioners, any questions on R3?
In the Lumpkin County project, are those firm customers?
Janie, just one quick question. All of these numbers that are going into multi-year projects,
does all of that contemplate leaving enough funds in there to do what we're doing on the low-income
heating assistance programs as well? Yes, sir. Okay, thank you. All right, any questions?
Janie, I understood from the committee meeting that there wasn't an alternative energy source
analysis done, but for USF proposals that include, like this one, two or more classes of customers,
do we typically provide the data on the percentage of total project costs that are attributable to
connecting each class of customer? Sorry, could you repeat the question for USF projects?
Yes, do we give the percentage of the total project costs that are attributable to connecting
these different class of customers? Is it less than 20% attributable
to the cost of connecting the farmers versus the industrial customers? I'm just trying to understand
the amounts for industrial class customers versus the farmers. Commissioner, no, we do not. We don't
do that type of analysis. It's just whatever is proposed for the project is what we review
based on the MFRs. Okay. All right. Well, thank y'all. All right, we'll move on
since there's no more questions. You've heard staff's recommendations on R3. All in favor,
say aye. Aye. Aye. All opposed? Nay. Nay. All right. The R3 passes with commissioners
Shaw, McDonald, Pride, more voting than the affirmative and commissioners Johnson and Hubbard
voting no. Okay. That concludes our regular agenda. Was there any other business to be taken up on
the utility agenda? All right. We'll move on to administrative affairs. We have a consent agenda
for administrative affairs. Does any commissioner wish to hold any item or move it from the consent
agenda to the regular agenda? If not, all in favor of approving the administrative affairs
consent agenda, say aye. Aye. Any opposed? All right. Administrative affairs consent agenda passes
unanimously. Is any other business to be taken up today? I want to remind everyone that we do have
a hearing to follow. We'll take a 10-minute break and retool IT and so forth. Thank y'all for being
with us and thank you for your patience while we finished our business this morning. We are
adjourned and we'll get, yes, this is your, this is your last.
